sources.quote: TAMPA, Fla., June 30, 2017 /PRNewswire/ -- TrueCore Behavioral Solutions, formerly G4S Youth Services, announces today the formal change of name and ownership of the multi-state operator of at-risk-youth residential facilities and outpatient services.

note: The board has this backwards. G4S sold its Youth Services subsidiary to an investment group that included its management (BHSB Holdings), and in June 2017 it was renamed TrueCore Behavioral Solutions.

sources.quote: Utah Girls Village's name was changed to Utah Youth Village at the end of 1989 due to the addition of boys to the Village's program.

note: Drawn backwards: Utah Girls' Village (founded 1969) became Utah Youth Village at the end of 1989, when it began taking boys. A search summary gave 1988 from another source that could not be verified; the organization's own policy manual says 1989.

Aspiro (Mt. Pleasant, UT), which ran Vantage Point, rebranded as ThreePeaks: aspiroadventure.com/who-we-help/vantage-point/ now 301-redirects to threepeakstreatment.com. No dated statement found, and the link between Vantage Point and the Beryl/Enterprise 'Ascent' program is not confirmed.

sources.quote: Walkabout Therapeutic Expeditions of Lehi, a program of Aspen Education Group, has changed its name to Outback Therapeutic Expeditions.

note: Aspen Education Group renamed the program to avoid confusion or trademark claims from another Utah wilderness program using 'walkabout'. The quote itself has no year; the year is the September 21, 2004 date of the Deseret News article. The program closed on June 15, 2023. Year 2004 dropped: no quote contains it.

sources.quote: Rebranded as West Ridge Academy in 2005, the school is applying to become a charter school named Eagle Summit Academy, which would receive public funding on a per-student basis.
In early 2005, it opened new, separate facilities for girls and changed its name to West Ridge Academy.

note: Board order is backwards: Utah Boys Ranch was renamed West Ridge Academy in early 2005 when it opened separate facilities for girls.

sources.quote: The 300-acre campus opened for the adolescent boys ranch program in Liberty Hill & named Westwood program.

note: Meridell's timeline puts this in 1967: the Liberty Hill boys ranch opened and was named the Westwood program. That reads as a boys ranch program named Westwood from the start, not a later rename, so no rename year is given.

sources.quote: Founded in 2021, Maple Hall Academy is a therapeutic boarding school nestled in the Shenandoah Valley set against the Blue Ridge Mountains of Virginia
Founded in 2011, Whetstone Academy is a CARF and COGNIA accredited therapeutic boarding school

note: Probably not a rename: Whetstone Academy (South Carolina, 2011) still runs under its own name, and Maple Hall Academy was a separate Virginia school founded in 2021 on the same website template, whose domain is now parked. They look like sister programs with shared leadership (John Singleton), so this edge may be an affiliation, not a rename.

sources.quote: Woodward Academy was founded in 1900 as Georgia Military Academy. Originally an all-male school, in 1964 it became coeducational and was renamed Woodward Academy in 1966.

note: Likely a board mix-up: the Woodward Academy that was once Georgia Military Academy is the College Park, GA prep school, renamed in 1966, so Georgia Military came first (swapped). The node here is Woodward Academy in Woodward, IA (YSI/Sequel/Vivant), which has no known Georgia Military connection. The edge probably should be removed.

sources.quote: The center's name officially changed for the last time to The Beloit Juvenile Correctional Facility on July 1, 1997.

note: This was the last state renaming. The state closed the facility in 2009 and moved its residents to the Kansas Juvenile Correctional Complex in Topeka.

sources.quote: Three Points Center is a WWASP-affiliated behavior modification that was founded in 2014
The program was originally located in the former location of Cross Creek Manor
as of October 13th 2013, Youth Foundation Success Academy (YFSA) will be ceasing operations.

note: Not a documented rename: YFSA closed October 2013, and Three Points Center was founded in 2014 on the same former Cross Creek Manor campus (moved to Hurricane in 2018). Successor on the same site, not a proven rebrand.
